spans.text:
- paragraph: Yep! A good rule-of-thumb that I learned is, once the pilea pup has about 4-5 leaves on its own - you’re good to go!
      - paragraph:
        - text: How to divide for propagation according to
        - link "House Plant Central":
          - /url: https://houseplantcentral.com/propagating-pilea-peperomioides-propagate-chinese-money-plant/
      - paragraph:
        - strong: Propagating From Root Plantlets
      - paragraph:
        - emphasis: The easiest way to propagate Pilea peperomioides is by using plantlets that grow from the mother plant’s roots. A healthy, large Pilea that has plenty of pot space should regularly produce these. They pop up from the soil and are ready to use once they have a few leaves of their own.
      - paragraph:
        - emphasis: Because root plantlets already have a root system of their own the only thing you have to do is sever their connection to the mother plant’s roots using a sharp and clean knife. Then, just pop them into smaller pots of their own and keep the soil lightly moist. Voila! Brand new Pilea peperomioides babies that you can keep, give away or sell. The move to their own pot might slightly shock the babies but because they already have a root system they usually immediately start growing.
      - paragraph: Goodluck & happy planting!

- paragraph: I typically wait until the baby’s leaves are quarter sized. The bigger the baby, the better your chances! I take a clean, sharp knife and cut it under the soil and put it into a tiny pot with well draining soil. Don’t bury it too deep.
